preamble: The close front vowel /i/ is lowered to close-mid [e] next to emphatic (pharyngealized) consonants. In Moroccan Arabic the full vowels /a i u/ are realized as [ɑ e o] in the vicinity of an emphatic consonant or q, χ, ʁ, r, and as [æ i u] elsewhere; emphasis spreads most reliably from a consonant to the vowel that directly follows it and towards the beginning of the word.

examples.note: Both /i/ and /a/ take their emphatic allophones before /dˤ/.

related.label: Parallel emphasis-conditioned vowel lowering for back vowels
